θεόν· τὸ δὲ διὰ τὸν θεὸν βουλεύεσθαι παραγενέσθαι οὐκ ἐλαφρίας. Βουλευόμενος
ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς κατεπαγγειλάμην ὑμῖν τοῦτο οὐχ ὑπὸ προπετείας καὶ
ἐλαφρότητος· οὐδὲ γὰρ ὃ βουλεύομαι κατὰ σάρκα βουλεύομαι ἀλλὰ πνευματικά.
πρέπει δὲ τὸν περὶ πνευματικῶν βουλευόμενον μηδαμοῦ διαψεύδεσθαι, ἵνα ᾖ παρ'
αὐτῷ τὸ ναὶ ναὶ καὶ τὸ οὒ οὔ. 2 Kor 1,18 Τὸ μὲν ἐλθεῖν ἢ μὴ οὐκ ἐν ἐμοί, τὸ δὲ
προθέσθαι ἐν ἐμοί. εἰ μὲν οὖν ναὶ καὶ οὒ εἶχε τὸ κήρυγμα, δικαίως εἶχέ μου ἡ βουλὴ
τῆς πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἀφίξεως ναὶ καὶ οὔ· εἰ δὲ ὁ λόγος ἀληθής, δι' ὅλου καὶ τὸ τῆς βουλῆς
ἀληθές. Πιστεύω τῷ θεῷ ὅτι οὐδὲν ὧν ἐκηρύξαμεν ψεῦδός ἐστιν. 2 Kor 1,19 Οὐδὲ γὰρ
ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ υἱὸς ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς ἐγένετο ψεύστης. 2 Kor 1,20–22 ∆ιὰ τοῦ
Χριστοῦ τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρὶ τὸ ἀμὴν ἀναπέμπομεν. τὴν δὲ εἰς Χριστὸν βεβαίωσιν διὰ
τοῦ θεοῦ ἐλάβομεν. διὰ δὲ τοῦ σφραγισάμενος ἡμᾶς ἐδήλωσεν ἡμῶν τὴν πρὸς τὸν
θεὸν 281 οἰκειότητα καὶ τὴν ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ ἀλλοτρίωσιν· καὶ γὰρ καὶ οἱ ποιμένες
σφραγῖδα τοῖς ποιμνίοις ἐπιτιθέασιν τὰ ἴδια αὐτῶν ἀπὸ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων
διακρίνοντες. εἰπὼν δὲ ἀρραβῶνα ἐνέφηνεν, ὅτι μικρόν τι ἐνέχυρον ἀπὸ τῆς
γνώσεως εἰλήφαμεν, τὸ δὲ τέλειον ἡμῖν κεχρεώστηται· ὁ γὰρ ἀρραβὼν μέρος ἐξ
ὅλου. 2 Kor 1,23–24 Ἐπειδὴ πολλὰ ἦν τὰ κατ' αὐτῶν ἐγκλήματα, οὐκ ἠβούλετο
ἀπελθὼν κατακρῖναι αὐτούς. Ἐλλειπῶς εἴρηται ὁ λόγος· θέλει γὰρ εἰπεῖν ὅτι
ἠβουλόμην ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἀλλ' οὐχ ὡς κύριός ἐστι καὶ διδάσκαλος τῆς ὑμετέρας
πίστεως. Τὸ μὲν πταῖσαι ὑμᾶς ἐν ὑμῖν, τὸ δὲ διορθῶσαι πταίοντας ἐν ἡμῖν, ἵνα
συνεργοὶ τῆς κατὰ θεὸν χαρᾶς γενώμεθα. Ἐν ὑμῖν τὸ πιστεῦσαι, ἐν ἡμῖν τὸ
διορθοῦσθαι τοὺς πταίοντας, ἵνα συνεργοὶ γενώμεθα τῆς χάριτος τοῦ θεοῦ. χαρὰν δὲ
τὴν κατὰ θεὸν λέγει· οὐ γὰρ ἂν αὐτοῖς εἰς κοσμικὴν χαρὰν συνήργησεν ὁ ἀπόστολος.
Εἰπὼν τῇ πίστει, ἐνέφηνεν ὅτι τοῖς ἔργοις ἀπολιμπάνονται. διὸ ὡς ἄκαρπον ἔχουσι
τὴν πίστιν καὶ ἔτι ἀτελὲς οὖσαν, συνεργὸν αὐτοῖς εἶναί φησιν. 2 Kor 2,1 ∆ιὰ τοῦτο
οὐκ ἦλθον, οὐχ ἵνα μὴ λυπήσω ὑμᾶς ἀλλ' ἐμαυτόν, καὶ ἵνα μή τινας κατακρίνω ἐφ'
οἷς πράττουσιν. 2 Kor 2,2 Οὐκ ἐκ τῶν ὁμοίων ὑμεῖς λυπεῖτέ με κἀγὼ ὑμᾶς· ὑμεῖς μὲν
γὰρ ἐξ ὧν ἁμαρτάνετε λυπεῖτέ με, ἐγὼ δὲ ἐξ ὧν ἐπιπλήττω λυπῶ ὑμᾶς. ἀλλὰ
εὐφραίνει ὁ λυπούμενος–ἔοικε γὰρ αἰσθόμενος λυπεῖσθαι–· ὁ γὰρ μὴ λυπηθεὶς δῆλον
ὡς οὐδ' ἐφρόντισεν ἐγκληθείς. εἰ γὰρ καὶ λυπῶ ὑμᾶς, ἁρμόδιον πρᾶγμα ποιῶ,
σύντεινον εἰς ἐμὴν εὐφροσύνην ἐπὶ τῇ ὑμετέρᾳ ὠφελείᾳ. 2 Kor 2,3 Τοῦτο ἔγραψα τὸ
ὅτι φειδόμενος ὑμῶν οὐκ ἦλθον, ἐν τῷ τέλει τῆς ἐπιστολῆς ταύτης ἔνθα κεῖται μή
πως ἐλθόντα με 282 ταπεινώσῃ ὁ θεός. καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἔγραψα, ἵνα ἐν ἡδονῇ ὑμᾶς
εὕρω διορθωθέντας ἵνα μὴ λυπῆσθε. οὐ τὸ ἐμαυτοῦ δὲ σκοπῶν τοῦτο εἶπον ἀλλὰ τὸ
ὑμέτερον· οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι ἐὰν ἴδητέ με χαίροντα χαίρετε, καὶ ἐὰν εἰδῆτέ με ἀλγοῦντα
ἀλγεῖτε. Ταῦτα ἔγραψα, ἵνα εἰ βούλεσθέ με ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, προδιορθώσησθε τὰ
πταίσματα. 2 Kor 2,4 ∆είξας ὅτι τὰ αὐτὰ πταίσματα ἴδια ποιεῖται, πένθη καὶ δάκρυα
ἐνέφηνεν ἣν ἔχει πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἀγάπην. εἰπὼν ἔγραψα ὑμῖν, οὐχ ἵνα ἁπλῶς
λυπηθῆτε, ἀλλ' ἵνα διαδέξηται τὴν λύπην ἡ κατὰ θεὸν χαρά. 2 Kor 2,5 Εἴ τις ἐμὲ καὶ
ἀγαπῶντα λελύπηκεν, οὐκ ἐμὲ μόνον λελύπηκεν ἀλλ' ἀπὸ μέρους καὶ ὑμᾶς, ἵνα μὴ
ἐπιβαρῶ λέγων καὶ τὸν Χριστόν· ἐσιώπησε δὲ τὸ εἰπεῖν «καὶ τὸν Χριστόν», ἵνα μὴ
καὶ εἰπὼν βαρήσῃ. 2 Kor 2,6 Ἐπιτιμίαν λέγει τὴν κατάγνωσιν τὴν ἐκ τῶν πλειόνων.
2 Kor 2,7 Χαρίσασθαι αὐτῷ τοῦτο. 2 Kor 2,8–9 Ὑπηκούσατέ μοι εἰς τὸ κατακρῖναι,
ὑπακούσατέ μοι καὶ εἰς τὸ ἀνακαλέσασθαι αὐτὸν κατακριθέντα. 2 Kor 2,10
Χαρίσασθε αὐτῷ, φησί, τοῦτο· γινώσκετε γὰρ ὅτι ὧν ὑμεῖς χαρίζεσθε τούτῳ κἀγὼ
βούλομαι χαρίζεσθαι. διὰ δὲ τούτου δείκνυσιν ὅτι ἐκ διαθέσεως τῆς περὶ αὐτοὺς τὰ
αὐτὰ αὐτοῖς φρονεῖν βούλεται. 2 Kor 2,12–13 Φαίνεται λυπηθεὶς πρὸς τοὺς ἐν
Τρῳάδι, ὅτι μὴ περὶ πολλοῦ ἐποίησαν τὸν Τίτον μηδὲ κατέσχον αὐτὸν ἕως τῆς αὐτοῦ
ἐπιδημίας, ἀλλ' ὡς χαῦνοι περὶ τὴν πίστιν εἴασαν ἀπελθεῖν. σωφρονίζων οὖν 283
αὐτοὺς ὡς ἀναξίους παρέδραμεν καίτοιγε θύρας ἀνεῳγμένης καὶ οὐδενὸς
ἀποκλείοντος τῷ κηρύγματι. ἤτοι καὶ διὰ τοῦτο παρέδραμεν ὡς ῥάδιον δυνάμενος
διορθώσασθαι τὰ ἐκεῖ ὕστερον ἐπιδημῶν ὡς οὐδενὸς ὄντος τοῦ παρεμποδίζοντος. 2
Kor 2,14 Τοῦτ' ἔστι τῷ δημοσιεύοντι ἡμῶν τὰς ὕβρεις καὶ τὰς περιστάσεις τὰς διὰ

pass_a_gloss:
[Continues the 1:17 note from the previous section: "...but on account of] God; and the planning to arrive on account of God is not a matter of lightness. Planning to come to you, I announced this to you not from rashness and lightness; for neither what I plan do I plan according to flesh, but spiritual things. And it befits the one planning about spiritual things never to be proved false, so that with him the yes may be yes and the no, no.
[Label 2 Cor 1:18.] The coming or not is not in me, but the purposing is in me. So if the preaching had yes and no, justly would my plan of arrival to you have had yes and no; but if the word is true, wholly the matter of the plan is also true. I trust God that nothing of the things we preached is a lie.
[Label 2 Cor 1:19.] For neither did the Son of God, our Lord Jesus, become a liar.
[Label 2 Cor 1:20-22.] Through Christ we send up the amen to God and Father. And the confirmation into Christ we received through God. And through "who sealed us" he made clear our belonging to God and our estrangement from the evil one; for shepherds too put a seal on their flocks, distinguishing their own from the others'. And by saying "pledge" he indicated that we have received some small security from the knowledge, but the complete is owed to us; for the pledge is a part out of a whole. [Page number 281 dropped.]
[Label 2 Cor 1:23-24.] Since the charges against them were many, he did not want, having gone away there, to condemn them. The statement is said elliptically; for he wants to say that "I wanted to come to you, but not as one is lord and teacher of your faith." The stumbling of you is in you, but the correcting of those stumbling is in us, so that we may become fellow workers of the joy according to God.
[Second catena form of the same note, not marked: "Believing is in you, correcting those who stumble is in us, so that we may become fellow workers of the grace of God." Its new material:] And he says joy, the one according to God; for the apostle would not have worked together with them toward worldly joy. [Then, still before the next label:] Having said "by faith," he hinted that they are left behind in works. Therefore, as they have the faith fruitless and still being incomplete, he says he is their fellow worker.
[Label 2 Cor 2:1.] On account of this I did not come, not in order that I may not grieve you but myself, and in order that I may not condemn some for the things they do.
[Label 2 Cor 2:2.] Not from like things do you grieve me and I you; for you grieve me from the things in which you sin, but I grieve you from the things in which I rebuke. But the one being grieved gladdens [me], for he seems to be grieved having perceived; for the one not grieved clearly did not even care when accused. For even if I grieve you, I do a fitting thing, tending toward my gladness at your benefit.
[Label 2 Cor 2:3.] I wrote this, the "that sparing you I did not come," at the end of this letter, where it lies "lest perhaps, when I have come, God humble me." [Page number 282 dropped.] And on account of this I wrote, in order that I may find you, with pleasure, set right, in order that you not be grieved. Not looking at my own did I say this, but at yours; for I know that if you see me rejoicing, you rejoice, and if you see me in pain, you are in pain. I wrote these things in order that, if you wish me to come to you, you may correct the stumbles beforehand.
[Label 2 Cor 2:4.] Having shown that he makes the same stumbles his own, by griefs and tears he revealed the love which he has toward them. Saying "I wrote to you": not in order that you be simply grieved, but in order that the joy according to God may succeed the grief.
[Label 2 Cor 2:5.] If anyone has grieved me, even loving, he has not grieved me only but in part you also, in order that I may not weigh down by saying "and Christ"; and he kept silent the saying "and Christ," so that by saying it he might not be heavy.
[Label 2 Cor 2:6.] He calls "punishment" the condemnation from the majority.
[Label 2 Cor 2:7.] To forgive him this.
[Label 2 Cor 2:8-9.] You obeyed me toward condemning; obey me also toward calling back the man condemned.
[Label 2 Cor 2:10.] "Forgive him this," he says; "for you know that the things you forgive this man, I also wish to forgive." And through this he shows that from his disposition toward them he wishes to think the same things as they.
[Label 2 Cor 2:12-13.] He appears grieved toward those in Troas, because they did not make much of Titus nor held him back until his own arrival, but as slack about the faith let him go away. So, bringing them to soundness of mind as unworthy, he ran past, although a door was opened and no one shutting out the preaching. Or he ran past also on account of this, as able easily to correct things there later when visiting, as there was nothing hindering. [Page number 283 dropped.]
[Label 2 Cor 2:14.] That is, to the one who makes public our insults and the hardships on account of Christ. And he confesses a greater grace in that he is deemed worthy to be led in triumph on account of Christ. And he says these things also on account of the Corinthians; for he feared lest they should give way on account of the ... [sentence continues in the next section]
pass_b_english: … God. To plan a visit for God's sake is no mark of fickleness. When I planned to come to you, I made you that promise, not out of rashness or lightness; for when I make plans, I do not make them according to the flesh: I plan spiritual things. And one who plans spiritual things must never prove false, so that with him yes is yes and no is no.

On 2 Corinthians 1:18: Whether I come or not does not rest with me; making the plan does. If the preaching had a yes and a no, my plan to come to you would rightly have had a yes and a no as well. But if the word is true, then the plan is true through and through. I trust God that nothing we have preached is false.
On 2 Corinthians 1:19: For the Son of God, our Lord Jesus, did not prove a liar either.

On 2 Corinthians 1:20–22: Through Christ we send up the Amen to God the Father, and through God we received our confirmation in Christ. By “who sealed us” he made plain that we belong to God and are estranged from the evil one; shepherds, too, set a seal on their flocks to tell their own sheep from other people's. By saying “pledge” he indicated that we have received a small security out of knowledge, while the full gift is still owed to us; for a pledge is a part of the whole.

On 2 Corinthians 1:23–24: Since the charges against them were many, he did not want to go there and condemn them. The sentence is elliptical. He means: I did want to come to you, but not as one who is lord and teacher of your faith. Stumbling is your affair; setting right those who stumble is ours, so that we may become fellow workers in the joy that is according to God.

The second catena form adds: By joy he means the joy that is according to God, for the apostle would not have worked with them toward a worldly joy. When he says “by faith,” he hints that they fall short in works. So, since their faith is still fruitless and incomplete, he says that he is their fellow worker.
On 2 Corinthians 2:1: This is why I did not come: not to keep from grieving you, but to keep from grieving myself, and so as not to condemn some for what they are doing.

On 2 Corinthians 2:2: You grieve me and I grieve you, but not for the same reasons. You grieve me by your sins; I grieve you by my rebukes. Yet the one who feels grief makes me glad, for his grief seems to show that he has understood; whoever feels no grief plainly did not care when he was accused. So even if I grieve you, I am doing the right thing, and it leads to my own gladness at your benefit.

On 2 Corinthians 2:3: “I wrote this,” that is, that I stayed away to spare you, at the end of this letter, where it says, “lest perhaps when I come God may humble me” (2 Corinthians 12:21). I wrote for this reason: to find you, to my pleasure, already set right, so that you would not be grieved. I said this with an eye to your good, not to mine; for I know that if you see me rejoicing, you rejoice, and if you see me in pain, you are in pain. I wrote these things so that, if you want me to come, you may correct your faults before I arrive.

On 2 Corinthians 2:4: Having shown that he makes their faults his own, he revealed by his mourning and his tears the love he has for them. When he says “I wrote to you,” he means: not that you should simply be grieved, but that joy according to God should take the place of your grief.

On 2 Corinthians 2:5: If anyone has grieved me, a man who loves, he has grieved not me alone but, in part, you as well. He stops there so as not to press too hard by adding “and Christ.” He kept back the words “and Christ,” so that saying them would not weigh too heavily.
On 2 Corinthians 2:6: By “punishment” he means the condemnation passed by the majority.
On 2 Corinthians 2:7: To forgive him this.
On 2 Corinthians 2:8–9: You obeyed me when I said to condemn him; obey me also when I say to call the condemned man back.

On 2 Corinthians 2:10: “Forgive him this,” he says, “for you know that whatever you forgive this man, I too want to forgive.” In this way he shows that his affection for them makes him want to be of one mind with them.

On 2 Corinthians 2:12–13: He seems to have been grieved with the people in Troas. They had not made much of Titus or kept him there until Paul himself arrived, but, slack about the faith, they let him go. So, to bring them to their senses as unworthy, he passed them by, even though a door had been opened and no one was shutting out the preaching. Or he passed them by for this reason as well: he could easily set things right there on a later visit, since nothing stood in the way.

On 2 Corinthians 2:14: That is, to him who makes public the insults and hardships we suffer for Christ. Paul confesses it a greater grace that he is counted worthy to be led in triumph because of Christ. He also says this for the Corinthians' sake, for he feared that they might give way because of the …
notes: 2026-11-11 claude-sumfix-b3: retranslated from the locked Greek. The old English was a word-order gloss, titled 'Severianus on 2 Corinthians 2' though it runs 1:17 to 2:14, printed the 1:24 note twice, and had a broken word and bare label in 2:10 ('ch', '2 Kor'). Title replaced. Doublet collapsed: 1:23-24 (first form kept; the second form reads 'believing rests with you' for 'stumbling' and 'grace of God' for 'joy according to God'; its new sentences, with the 'by faith' note that follows it, are printed under 'The second catena form adds:'). Labels now one per note (1:18 to 2:14); page numbers 281-283 dropped; section opens and ends mid-sentence with '…'.

choices.why: The Greek begins mid-sentence, finishing the 1:17 note ('but because of God') from the end of u01-open.
The Greek is whole; the old English had a broken word ('ch') and a bare '2 Kor' label.

choices.english: first form kept; second printed only for its new sentences under 'The second catena form adds:'
choices.why: The second form repeats the first with two word changes ('believing' for 'stumbling', 'grace of God' for 'joy according to God'); those variants are recorded here and in translator_notes, not printed twice.

choices.term: Εἰπὼν τῇ πίστει ... συνεργὸν αὐτοῖς εἶναί φησιν
choices.why: It follows the second form in the edition before the next label; the edition does not mark where that form ends, so it is left in sequence and nothing is moved.
